entries.title: CoSnitch (CVE-2026-24301): Microsoft Copilot Personal Patches Critical One-Click Data Exfiltration Flaw — Discovered via 'Meta-Hacking' the Model Itself
entries.summary: Varonis disclosed and Microsoft patched a critical vulnerability in Copilot Personal (CVE-2026-24301) that allowed attackers to silently exfiltrate data from connected OAuth apps (Gmail, Drive, OneDrive) with a single malicious link — the exploit was discovered by prompting Copilot to explain why auto-execution was impossible until it mapped its own attack surface, a technique Varonis calls 'meta-hacking.'

links.title: Computerworld — eight months from report to full patch

entries.title: arXiv 2608.17202 (Fool's Gold): Decoy Hardening Makes Safety-Stripped Open-Weight Models Return Fluent but Falsified Hazardous Answers
entries.summary: Rather than preventing abliteration of open-weight model safety alignments (which is trivially easy), 'Fool's Gold' accepts that refusal will be stripped and instead poisons the post-abliteration state so that hazardous queries yield confident-sounding decoys with falsified critical details — tested on seven models from five families, achieving 0.51–0.90 decoy rates on attacked-state responses while preserving clean-state utility.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.17445: Decomposition Attacks Across Unlinkable Identities — Stateful LLM Defenses Provably Fail When Attackers Use Fresh Identities
entries.summary: A formal and empirical study proves that decomposition attacks (splitting a harmful task across individually-permissible requests and combining answers elsewhere) achieve ≥99% success after one attempt and 100% after two on defense-unseen task families, because unlinkable fresh identities eliminate the grouping signal that any stateful monitor requires — closing the defense with identity-linkage costs or answer-use controls is identified as the only viable path.

entries.title: White House Finalizes Voluntary Frontier AI Safety Testing Program With Meta, Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI
entries.summary: The White House has finalized a voluntary safety testing program for advanced U.S. AI models — inviting Meta, Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI to participate in government-coordinated pre-release evaluations covering national-security risk assessment and third-party model evaluation — establishing a de facto pre-deployment review baseline ahead of any mandatory framework.

entries.title: Stanford/MIT AI Observatory: Vendor AI Usage Reports Systematically Filter Harmful Behavior, Leaving Enterprise Risk Assessments Structurally Incomplete
entries.summary: An independent platform led by Stanford and MIT researchers analyzed over 24,000 real AI conversations and found that usage reports published by major AI companies systematically exclude non-work-related interactions, concealing materially higher rates of harassment, hate speech, and adult content — meaning compliance programs relying on vendor-published data are working from a structurally incomplete picture.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.17597 (HarnessRisk): Agent Harness Safety Benchmark — Attack Success 12.6%–80.9% Across 14 Configurations; Explicit Risk Recognition Does Not Prevent Unsafe Actions
entries.summary: HarnessRisk organizes agent harness safety into six lifecycle phases (Configuration, Capability Extension, Runtime Operation, State Persistence, Action Control, Incident Recovery) with 128 sandboxed adversarial cases, finding that Harness Configuration is the most vulnerable phase across all three tested harnesses, and that configurations detecting risk in >90% of runs still retain substantial attack success rates.

entries.title: Fake Think Tank (Hanover Institute) Created by Israeli Government Contractor to Poison LLM Training Data — Live Example of 'AI Story Optimization' as Influence Operation
entries.summary: A fabricated organization called the Hanover Institute, created by contractor Piro, Inc. on behalf of the Israeli Government Advertising Agency, has published over 100 AI-generated reports since August 2026 explicitly to shape how LLMs evaluate source credibility on the Israel-Palestine conflict — Piro markets this as 'AI Story Optimization,' representing a documented live case of deliberate LLM training-data poisoning.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.17659 (MobileWorldSafety): GUI Agents on Android Remain Highly Vulnerable to Environmental Injection — Attack Success 40.4%–66.9% Across Six Agents
entries.summary: MobileWorldSafety introduces a benchmark of 142 risk tasks on real Android apps with programmatically verifiable outcomes, finding that all six evaluated agents (including both general and specialized GUI agents) are highly vulnerable to environmental injection attacks embedded in ordinary mobile content, with all attack success rates between 40.4% and 66.9%.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.17360 (Fair ASR): Jailbreak Attack Rankings Reverse Under Shared Query Budgets — ReCode Achieves 85% ASR on GPT-5 in 20 Calls
entries.summary: Fair-ASR introduces a compute-normalized jailbreak evaluation protocol that uses target-model calls as a method-agnostic comparison axis, finding that attack rankings change substantially across budgets, that simple stochastic perturbations remain highly competitive under equal access, and that a new compositional attack (ReCode) reaches 85% ASR on GPT-5 in 20 target calls using only 7.19 attacker calls per request on average.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.16177 (v2): Milgram Paradigm Applied to 42 LLMs — Full-Obedience Rates Span 0%–100%, Are Model-Specific and Stable, But Do Not Track Lineage
entries.summary: A standardized Milgram obedience paradigm run across 4,848 sessions and 42 models from 19 families finds that baseline full-obedience rates are extremely heterogeneous (census mean 42.9%; human anchor 65%), that profiles are model-specific and stable (split-half AUC 0.885) yet do not recover model lineage — and that declaring a scenario fictional raises obedience, while native tool-call framing and a thinking budget both lower it sharply.

entries.title: OpenAI Launches Teen-Specific ChatGPT With Default Content Restrictions and Parental Notifications — Triggering Education-Sector Vendor Governance Reassessments
entries.summary: OpenAI has launched a teen version of ChatGPT with default content restrictions, a Study Mode feature, and parental notification tools — years after minors began using the general product without age-specific safeguards — creating an immediate obligation for education and edtech compliance teams to reassess vendor contracts and intake processes.

entries.title: OWASP GenAI and CoSAI Publish Concurrent Agentic AI Security Baselines — MCP Server Security Guide and Token-Exchange Standard
entries.summary: OWASP GenAI published a practical MCP server security guide covering authentication, authorization, session isolation, and input validation, while the Coalition for Secure AI simultaneously published guidance establishing token exchange at every agent trust boundary as a foundational control principle — together providing the first concurrent multi-organization security baseline for enterprise agentic deployments.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.17583: Cross-National Sockpuppet Audit of TikTok Harmful Content — Keyword Search Delivers 35–56% Harmful Content, Up to 7.5× the Passive Scrolling Baseline
entries.summary: Using MLLM-based annotation (Gemini 2.5 Flash, validated against native-speaker labels), a sockpuppet audit of TikTok across France, Italy, and Sweden with four age personas (13, 16, 19, 40) finds that active keyword search for harm spikes harmful content to 35–56% — a 1.5–7.5× increase over passive scrolling — while the platform's safety filters refusal rate of only 1.1% under-counts the most explicit harms.
